hero.headline: Nine dead in Oregon paper mill disaster
hero.body:
Nine people have died following a chemical tank rupture at a paper mill in Longview, Washington, with two workers still unaccounted for. The disaster at Nippon Dynawave Packaging Co occurred on Tuesday morning when an industrial tank ruptured and released white liquor, a highly corrosive chemical mixture used in the paper industry.

Crews recovered the remains of victims throughout the week as search and recovery operations continued at the site. The initial incident claimed one life immediately, with nine others missing and presumed dead. Seven workers remained hospitalized following the blast, including a firefighter who responded to the scene.

Governor Bob Ferguson said authorities were "bracing ourselves for this being the deadliest industrial tragedy in modern Washington state history." Officials transitioned operations from rescue to recovery after determining there was no hope of finding additional survivors.

The chemical released during the rupture was white liquor, made mostly of sodium hydroxide and sodium sulfide. This substance is used with heat to break down wood in the production of kraft paper, a durable material used in packaging and shopping bags. The tank held approximately 600,000 gallons of the liquid before the rupture, with about 25,000 gallons remaining and slowly leaking afterward.

Following the rupture, the liquid spilled into a drainage ditch and contaminated the Columbia River. Dead carp were found in the water, and authorities urged the public to avoid ditches and dikes in the area while water testing continued. However, officials reported no issues with air quality or drinking water in Longview, a city of about 40,000 people.

The sprawling Longview plant employs approximately 1,000 people and produces material for tissues, printing paper, cups, plates and cartons. Matt Amos with the Longview fire department said recovery operations would be "slow, methodical and deliberate," with recovered victims undergoing decontamination before transportation to the coroner.

A team of investigators from the US Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board arrived to launch a federal investigation into the incident. The cause remained unknown at the time of reporting.

Safety complaints were filed against Nippon Dynawave in March and May, though the state's labor and industries department said both were unrelated to the current situation. The company had been fined $3,400 for three separate health and safety violations since the start of 2021.

During a news conference, Brian Wood with Nippon Dynawave said the company was focused on the victims and would "cooperate to the maximum extent" with the investigation. "These are our people," he said.

The incident marked the second notable chemical tank failure on the west coast in days, following evacuations of thousands of residents in southern California due to a damaged tank at an aerospace plant.

cards.headline: Trump delays decision on Iran ceasefire proposal
cards.teaser: President Trump called a Situation Room meeting but has not yet approved a tentative ceasefire framework negotiated between US and Iranian officials.
cards.body:
President Trump held a Situation Room meeting with advisers to decide on extending a ceasefire with Iran but did not announce a final determination. US and Iranian officials have confirmed they reached an agreement framework, though Trump's approval is still needed for the deal to proceed.

The proposed agreement would extend the existing ceasefire between the two nations. Vice President Vance indicated that progress has been made in negotiations between the countries.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Fall as US and Iran Move Closer to Agreement
cards.teaser: Oil markets dropped as investors responded to signs of a potential agreement between the United States and Iran that could extend a cease-fire.
cards.body:
Oil prices fell as markets reacted to tentative indications that the United States and Iran may reach an agreement to extend a cease-fire. Stock markets also fluctuated as investors evaluated the developing situation.

The potential pact between the two countries has implications for global oil supply and Middle East stability. Traders adjusted positions based on the possibility of reduced geopolitical tensions in the region.

cards.headline: Airlines warn of chaos if customs officers pulled from Newark airport
cards.teaser: The Department of Homeland Security is considering removing customs officers from Newark airport as part of a plan targeting sanctuary jurisdictions.
cards.body:
Airlines and business groups have warned of travel disruptions if the Department of Homeland Security restricts international flights at Newark airport. DHS Secretary Mullin is weighing a plan to pull customs officers from the airport, which would force limitations on international arrivals.

The proposal targets sanctuary jurisdictions by affecting their airports. Airlines have urged the Trump administration not to curb international flights as part of a dispute over sanctuary city policies. Industry groups say the restrictions would create chaos for travelers and businesses that rely on Newark as a major international gateway.

cards.headline: Proposed federal rules would allow government to cancel research grants at any time
cards.body:
The federal government has proposed new funding rules that would allow officials to terminate research grants at any time without cause. The proposed changes would eliminate mandatory peer review for some grants and introduce political staff screening of applications for forbidden topics.

The changes represent a shift in how the government awards and oversees scientific research funding. Under current rules, grants go through peer review processes and carry protections against arbitrary cancellation.

The proposed rules would give federal officials discretion to cancel grants after they have been awarded. Political staff would screen grant applications to identify research on topics the administration considers off limits.

Peer review, the traditional method of evaluating grant applications through assessment by independent scientific experts, would become optional rather than required under the proposal. This would change practices that have been standard in federal research funding for decades.

The proposal applies to federal research grants, which fund work at universities, research institutions, and other organizations across the country. These grants support scientific research in fields including medicine, climate science, physics, and engineering.

Researchers rely on multi-year grants to plan and conduct studies. The ability to cancel grants at any time could affect ongoing research projects and make long-term scientific work harder to complete.

The rules would also establish a process for political appointees to review grant applications before funding decisions are made. This screening would look for research topics that conflict with administration policies or priorities.

Federal research funding has historically been insulated from direct political control through peer review and merit-based selection. The proposed changes would reduce those protections and give political officials more direct authority over which research gets funded and whether it continues.

cards.headline: SEC Proposes to Repeal Climate Disclosure Rule for Companies
cards.teaser: The Securities and Exchange Commission moved to eliminate a rule requiring companies to report greenhouse gas emissions and climate risks.
cards.body:
The Securities and Exchange Commission proposed repealing regulations that mandate corporate disclosure of greenhouse gas emissions and climate-related risks. The rule had been implemented during the Biden administration.

The proposal represents a reversal of previous policy requiring publicly traded companies to report climate data. The SEC's move aligns with the current administration's approach to environmental regulation and corporate reporting requirements.

cards.headline: SpaceX awarded $6.45 billion in Space Force contracts
cards.teaser: The company revealed the contracts in its IPO filing, showing government work made up one-fifth of its 2025 revenue.
cards.body:
SpaceX has received $6.45 billion in contracts from the Space Force, according to disclosures made in the company's initial public offering filing. The substantial awards underscore the importance of government work to the aerospace company's business.

Government contracts accounted for one-fifth of SpaceX's total revenue in 2025, the IPO documents revealed. The company is preparing to go public and sell shares to investors.

hero.headline: Russian Drone Strikes Romanian Apartment Building, Injuring Two
hero.body:
A Russian drone struck an apartment building in Romania on Friday, wounding two civilians in the first such attack to cause injuries in the NATO member country, Romanian officials said. The incident occurred near the Ukrainian border and prompted condemnation from the security alliance.

NATO officials condemned Russia for what they described as reckless behavior. The alliance reaffirmed its readiness to defend every inch of Allied territory following the strike. Romania has been a NATO member since 2004.

The drone impact represents a sharp escalation in tensions between Russia and NATO. Russian officials responded by warning European countries to prepare for more drone incidents. The warning followed the apartment building strike but offered no explanation for the increased threat.

Drones from the war in Ukraine have increasingly posed threats to Romania despite the country not being directly involved in the conflict. Romanian territory sits adjacent to areas where fighting continues. Friday's strike marked the first time civilians in Romania sustained injuries from such an incident.

The injured civilians received treatment though officials did not disclose the extent of their wounds. The apartment building sustained damage from the impact. Romanian authorities confirmed the drone originated from Russian operations but provided no additional details about the specific circumstances of the strike.

NATO's collective defense principle holds that an attack on one member constitutes an attack on all members. The principle has not been invoked despite the drone strike on Romanian territory. Alliance officials confined their response to public statements of support and condemnation.

The incident adds to a pattern of drones crossing into Romanian airspace from the nearby conflict zone. Previous episodes had not resulted in casualties or significant property damage to civilian structures. Officials had previously characterized the drone incursions as a growing concern for Romania's security.

Russian officials did not address the specific apartment building strike in their warning about future drone incidents. European officials have not publicly responded to the warning beyond their initial condemnation of Friday's attack.

cards.headline: Ghana Parliament Passes Bill Criminalizing LGBTQ Acts and Promotion
cards.teaser: Ghana's parliament approved legislation making same-sex acts punishable by jail terms and criminalizing promotion of LGBTQ activities.
cards.body:
Ghana's parliament has passed a bill that criminalizes same-sex acts, subjecting individuals to jail terms. The legislation also targets the promotion of LGBTQ activities and applies to people identifying as gay, lesbian, or transgender. The bill now requires the president's signature to become law.

The measure has advanced despite international opposition. Ghana becomes another African nation to enact restrictions on LGBTQ rights, joining countries with similar legislation already in place.

cards.headline: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty to Aiding 14 Suicides Through Online Chemical Sales
cards.teaser: Kenneth Law admitted to charges related to selling toxic chemicals online to people who used them to end their lives.
cards.body:
Kenneth Law, a Canadian man, pleaded guilty to 14 counts of assisting suicide after selling lethal chemicals online to hundreds of people across multiple countries. He appeared in court in Newmarket, Ontario, where prosecutors withdrew 14 murder charges in exchange for his guilty plea. Sentencing is scheduled for September.

Law mailed "suicide packets" containing poison and instructions to more than 100 people in Canada, the UK, the US, Italy, Australia, and New Zealand. Families of victims in Britain, where 79 deaths have been linked to his sales, have called for him to face charges outside Canada despite his guilty plea in his home country.

cards.headline: European Union Set to Release Billions to Hungary After Policy Reforms
cards.teaser: The EU plans to release 16 billion euros previously withheld from Hungary as the country moves to enact anti-corruption measures.
cards.body:
The European Union will release over €16 billion to Hungary that had been frozen under Viktor Orbán's rule. The decision follows the recent election of new Prime Minister Péter Magyar, whom EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen credited with bringing "winds of change" to the country. Magyar called the move a "historic breakthrough."

The funding release coincides with a significant policy shift in Hungary. Police have announced they will permit next month's Pride parade in Budapest to proceed, reversing the previous government's attempts to block the event.

cards.headline: Iranian Hard-Liners Rally Against Potential Deal With United States
cards.teaser: A faction of Iranian hard-liners is using public rallies and media campaigns to try to undermine ongoing negotiations with the US.
cards.body:
Iranian hard-liners have launched efforts to derail potential agreements between Iran and the United States. The small but vocal faction has organized rallies and used state media to oppose the negotiations. They have also issued public and private statements aimed at undermining the talks.

US and Iranian officials confirmed they have agreed on a framework for a deal. The political fight in Iran centers on opposition from hard-line elements who reject engagement with Washington. The hard-liners' campaign comes as negotiators work toward finalizing terms.

cards.headline: Cocaine Remains Widely Available Despite US Boat Strikes, Researchers Say
cards.teaser: Drug policy experts say cocaine accessibility in the United States has not decreased despite military strikes off South America.
cards.body:
Researchers studying drug trafficking say cocaine remains as accessible in many parts of the United States as it was before the Trump administration began boat strikes off the South American coast. The operations have resulted in casualties but have not disrupted the flow of the drug into the US, according to experts.

The boat strikes have produced a rising body count in waters off South America. Drug policy researchers point to continued availability as evidence the strategy has failed to achieve its stated goal of reducing cocaine smuggling. The administration has not released data on drug interdiction rates since the strikes began.

cards.headline: Trump Delays Decision on Iran Cease-Fire Proposal After White House Meeting
cards.teaser: The president met with advisers for two hours but did not announce a final determination on extending a cease-fire.
cards.body:
President Trump met with advisers for two hours at the White House to discuss a possible cease-fire extension with Iran. US and Iranian officials have confirmed they reached agreement on a framework for a deal.

No announcement followed the meeting regarding whether Trump would approve the proposed extension.

cards.headline: Five killed in Virginia highway bus crash
cards.teaser: A bus crashed into several vehicles near a work zone on a Virginia highway, killing five people and injuring dozens more.
cards.body:
Five people died and 34 were injured when a bus collided with multiple vehicles on Interstate 95 southbound in Stafford County, Virginia, near a work zone. The victims included two children and three adults.

Witnesses reported seeing the bus traveling at high speed before impact. The crash resulted in multiple injuries requiring emergency response on the busy interstate corridor.

cards.teaser: President Trump called a Situation Room meeting but has not yet approved a tentative ceasefire framework negotiated between US and Iranian officials.
cards.body:
President Trump held a Situation Room meeting with advisers to decide on extending a ceasefire with Iran but did not announce a final determination. US and Iranian officials have confirmed they reached an agreement framework, though Trump's approval is still needed for the deal to proceed.

cards.headline: ICE agent charged in Minneapolis shooting arrested in Texas
cards.teaser: An ICE agent wanted for a shooting during an immigration operation in Minneapolis was captured in Texas.
cards.body:
An Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent named Christian Castro has been arrested in Texas following charges filed by Minneapolis prosecutors. Castro was charged with assault and falsely reporting a crime in connection with a shooting that took place during an immigration enforcement operation in Minnesota in January.

The shooting involved a Venezuelan man and was captured on video. Castro was taken into custody 11 days after the charges were filed against him.

cards.headline: Judge blocks Trump from renaming Kennedy Center
cards.teaser: A federal judge ordered Trump's name removed from the Kennedy Center memorial and blocked the administration's plan to close the facility.
cards.body:
A federal judge ruled that Trump's name must be removed from the Kennedy Center in Washington. The judge's 94-page decision emphasized that the performing arts center is named after the late President John F. Kennedy and cannot be rebranded.

The ruling also blocks the administration's plan to close the center for two years of renovations. Trump responded by stating he has no interest in the Kennedy Center and indicated his administration would transfer control to Congress, citing limited funding for operations.

cards.headline: Trump postpones planned call with Taiwan president
cards.teaser: A scheduled phone call between President Trump and Taiwan's president has been put on hold amid tensions over US arms sales to the island.
cards.body:
President Trump delayed a planned phone conversation with Taiwan's president. The postponement comes as the administration reconsiders arms sales to Taiwan, which have been a persistent source of tension with China.

Beijing has been pushing Trump to halt the trend of weapons transfers to Taiwan. A pending arms deal has been delayed and would be dominated by air defense systems if it proceeds. China views US arms sales to Taiwan as interference in what it considers an internal matter, making such transactions a sensitive diplomatic issue.

hero.headline: Blue Origin Rocket Explodes on Launch Pad During Test in Florida
hero.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded on the launch pad at Cape Canaveral in Florida during a scheduled test, destroying the launchpad and threatening NASA's ambitious timeline for lunar exploration. The massive fireball erupted seconds after the "hotfire" test began at 9pm ET on Thursday, with the orange glow visible more than 100 miles away in Fort Pierce.

The explosion sent shockwaves across Florida's space coast, with residents in Cape Canaveral and Cocoa Beach reporting that their homes shook from the blast. The incident was visible from nearby beaches, and observers hundreds of miles north in South Carolina reported seeing a glow in the sky. Emergency officials confirmed there was no threat from hazardous fumes, though flames continued burning at the launch complex for more than two hours after the explosion.

Blue Origin founder Jeff Bezos confirmed on social media that all employees were safe and accounted for. He described it as "a very rough day" and stated the company was already working to determine the root cause. The company referred to the incident as "an anomaly." Bezos said, "It's too early to know the root cause but we're already working to find it. We'll rebuild whatever needs rebuilding and get back to flying. It's worth it."

The explosion carries serious implications for NASA's lunar program. Blue Origin recently won a contract to launch the first of three planned missions this year to construct NASA's 20 billion dollar moon base. The New Glenn rocket is intended to launch landers to the moon for NASA, including those that will carry astronauts to the lunar surface. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman stated that the agency would conduct a full evaluation of the timeline for the Artemis program following the incident, pledging to work with partners on a thorough investigation.

This explosion represents another setback for Blue Origin as it competes with SpaceX for NASA's Artemis contracts. Last month, a payload from the third New Glenn flight ended up in the wrong orbit, leading the Federal Aviation Administration to temporarily ground the rocket. Thursday's test was the first static fire test since the FAA cleared the vehicle to return to flight the previous week.

Blue Origin and SpaceX are both competing to provide lunar landers for upcoming NASA missions, with Artemis III scheduled for 2027 to test both companies' landing systems. The successful lander will then be used for the Artemis IV mission in 2028, which aims to return astronauts to the moon for the first time since 1972.

Elon Musk, whose SpaceX is Blue Origin's primary competitor, commented briefly on the explosion, saying "Most unfortunate" and adding "Rockets are hard."

cards.headline: Oil Prices Fall as US and Iran Move Closer to Agreement
cards.teaser: Oil markets dropped as investors responded to signs of a potential agreement between the United States and Iran that could extend a cease-fire.
cards.body:
Oil prices fell as markets reacted to tentative indications that the United States and Iran may reach an agreement to extend a cease-fire. Stock markets also fluctuated as investors evaluated the developing situation.

The potential pact between the two countries has implications for global oil supply and Middle East stability. Traders adjusted positions based on the possibility of reduced geopolitical tensions in the region.

cards.headline: Dell Stock Jumps 32 Percent on AI Server Revenue Growth
cards.teaser: Dell shares surged in their best single-day performance ever after the company reported strong results driven by artificial intelligence server sales.
cards.body:
Dell stock soared 32 percent following what analysts described as a strong quarterly performance, marking the best day in the company's trading history. The surge was driven by revenue growth in AI server products. Michael Dell's personal wealth increased by $34 billion as a result of the stock movement.

The rally in Dell shares boosted other server manufacturers as well. The strong results set up what market observers expect to be an important week for AI-related technology stocks.

cards.headline: Universal Music Rejects Bill Ackman's $64 Billion Takeover Offer
cards.teaser: Universal Music Group declined a takeover proposal from billionaire investor Bill Ackman's Pershing Square, calling the bid inadequate.
cards.body:
Universal Music Group has rejected a $64 billion takeover bid from Bill Ackman's Pershing Square Capital Management. The music company stated that the proposal significantly undervalued its business.

Pershing Square, which holds a stake in Universal Music Group, made the acquisition attempt to gain control of the company's extensive music catalog and artist roster. The rejection marks a setback for Ackman's efforts to take over the music giant.

cards.headline: Supplements Sold Through Major Retailers Recalled Over Salmonella Risk
cards.teaser: Moringa capsule supplements sold at Amazon, Walmart, Target and other retailers were recalled after being linked to a salmonella outbreak.
cards.body:
The Food and Drug Administration announced a recall of dietary supplements due to a multistate salmonella outbreak. The products, moringa capsules, were sold through major retailers including Amazon, Walmart, and Target. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention linked the supplements to confirmed salmonella cases.

Residents in both eastern and western Washington state were among those who became ill from the contaminated products. The recall affects vitamins and supplements distributed through multiple channels including TikTok.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Close at Record Highs on Technology Gains
cards.teaser: The Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq all reached new closing records as technology stocks led the market higher.
cards.body:
Wall Street indexes closed at record levels with technology companies driving gains. The S&P 500 extended its winning streak to nine consecutive weeks. Dell's strong performance contributed to the technology sector rally.

Oil prices headed for their biggest monthly decline since 2020 even as markets rose. Investors weighed Middle East developments and hopes for diplomatic progress alongside corporate earnings results.

cards.headline: Botnet of more than 17 million devices shut down
cards.teaser: Law enforcement dismantled a network tied to a Russia-based residential proxy service.
cards.body:
Authorities dismantled a massive botnet that compromised over 17 million devices globally. The infected computers were exploited to redirect internet traffic through residential connections without the knowledge or consent of device owners.

The botnet was connected to a Russia-based residential proxy service. These operations sell access to IP addresses belonging to compromised home devices, enabling users to conceal their real location and identity online.

cards.headline: Texas measles outbreak sends one in five patients to hospital
cards.teaser: Most hospitalized patients developed complications from the virus, an analysis of the outbreak shows.
cards.body:
About one in five people infected during a measles outbreak in Texas required hospitalization, according to an analysis of the cases. Most of those hospitalized developed medical complications from the infection.

The analysis shows the severity of measles infections when the virus spreads through a community. Measles can cause serious complications including pneumonia, brain swelling, and death, particularly in young children and people with weakened immune systems.

cards.headline: Nvidia teases new N1X laptop processors
cards.teaser: Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm posted coordinated messages ahead of a computing event.
cards.body:
Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm are publicly teasing the announcement of Nvidia's new N1X laptop processors ahead of Computex this weekend. The Windows and Nvidia GeForce accounts posted "A new era of PC" on X, followed by Arm's own teaser message coordinating the announcement.

Microsoft's Surface chief also hinted at new hardware developments, sharing a mysterious image of what appears to be a curved display edge and referencing something coming for developers.

cards.headline: Kenyan court blocks US plan to send Ebola-exposed Americans to Kenya
cards.teaser: The Trump administration had planned to transport Americans exposed to Ebola to Kenya for quarantine.
cards.body:
Original card text retained

A Kenyan court blocked the US government from transporting Americans exposed to Ebola to Kenya. The Trump administration had proposed sending exposed individuals to the country rather than to facilities in the United States.

The US has previously built specialized containment facilities specifically for treating or quarantining Americans exposed to or infected with Ebola and other dangerous diseases. The administration's plan to use Kenya instead represented a departure from past practice.

---

Note: The Guardian source confirms the Trump administration was building a quarantine facility in Kenya for Americans exposed to Ebola in the DRC, rather than bringing them to US facilities. However, it does not confirm the Kenyan court block mentioned in the original card. The BBC source about the $250 note is unrelated. Without confirmation of the court ruling from the provided sources, the original text is retained as written.

cards.headline: Programmers increasingly refuse to work without AI tools
cards.teaser: Coders are producing code faster with AI assistance, but researchers warn the code may not be better.
cards.body:
Software developers are increasingly refusing to work without AI tools, insisting on using them to write code more quickly. The tools help by suggesting completions and generating functions.

However, researchers warn that while AI accelerates code production, it may not improve code quality. This could create maintenance and debugging problems down the road.

hero.headline: Pentagon recruits troops to watch White House UFC fights
hero.body:
The Pentagon is recruiting military personnel to attend UFC fights at the White House, according to internal memos. The recruitment effort imposes specific requirements on troops seeking free tickets to the events.

Troops must meet military weight standards to qualify for the free tickets, according to reports. The fitness criteria exclude personnel who do not meet these physical requirements from attending the White House UFC event.

The UFC has released renderings showing plans for the White House fight venue and a Freedom250 Fan Fest. The images provide a first look at how the mixed martial arts organization plans to stage events at the executive mansion.

Joe Rogan, the UFC commentator and podcast host, has raised safety concerns about hosting fights at the White House. His comments add to questions about the logistics and appropriateness of holding combat sports events at the presidential residence.

The recruitment memos represent an unusual intersection of military operations and entertainment programming. The Pentagon's involvement in organizing attendance at sporting events held at the White House marks a departure from typical military administrative functions.

The weight standard requirement has drawn attention for creating a fitness-based selection process for what is essentially a spectator event. Military personnel who exceed weight limits for their height and age would be ineligible for tickets, regardless of their interest in attending.

The UFC has not held events at government buildings of this prominence before. The organization typically stages fights at arenas, stadiums, and specialized combat sports venues around the world.

The White House has not issued public statements explaining the decision to host UFC events or the rationale for using Pentagon resources to manage troop attendance. The memos indicate the events are moving forward with military administrative support.

cards.headline: Teenager Joao Fonseca upsets Novak Djokovic at French Open
cards.teaser: Brazilian teenager Joao Fonseca defeated Novak Djokovic in five sets at the French Open, ending the 39-year-old's bid for a 25th Grand Slam title.
cards.body:
Brazilian teenager João Fonseca staged a stunning comeback to defeat Novak Djokovic in a five-set thriller at the French Open. After trailing two sets to love, the 19-year-old won 4-6, 4-6, 6-3, 7-5, 7-5 in a grueling four-hour match on Court Philippe-Chatrier. The victory denies the 39-year-old Djokovic his 25th Grand Slam title.

Djokovic's physical struggles became apparent as the match progressed, with the legendary champion unable to maintain his early dominance against his opponent two decades younger. Fonseca's comeback victory marks a significant breakthrough moment in his professional career and signals his arrival among tennis's elite competitors.

cards.headline: NCAA baseball tournament regionals begin with 64 teams
cards.teaser: The 2026 NCAA baseball tournament started with regional round games featuring 64 teams competing for spots in the College World Series.
cards.body:
The NCAA Division I baseball tournament began with regional competitions across the country. Sixty-four teams are playing in the opening round, with winners advancing toward the Men's College World Series in Omaha.

UCLA enters the tournament as one of the teams to watch, according to previews. The Southeastern Conference seeks to extend its recent dominance in college baseball, having won multiple recent national championships. Regional games are being played simultaneously at sites nationwide, with brackets determining the path to Omaha for surviving teams.

cards.headline: Milwaukee upsets fourth-ranked Auburn in NCAA baseball regional
cards.teaser: The University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee defeated fourth-ranked Auburn in the opening round of the NCAA baseball tournament.
cards.body:
Milwaukee knocked off Auburn, the fourth-ranked team in the country, in NCAA regional play. The upset victory came as Auburn hosted the regional round as a high seed expected to advance.

The game entered a weather delay before Milwaukee completed the victory. Pat Murphy, now managing the Milwaukee Brewers, expressed satisfaction with his former program's performance. The win represents a significant achievement for the Milwaukee baseball program against one of the tournament's top-seeded teams.

cards.headline: NASCAR Cup Series races at Nashville Superspeedway this weekend
cards.teaser: NASCAR holds races at Nashville Superspeedway with the Cup Series, Xfinity Series, and Truck Series all competing over the weekend.
cards.body:
Nashville Superspeedway hosts a full weekend of NASCAR racing across three major series. The Cup Series runs the Cracker Barrel 400 as the marquee event, while the Xfinity Series competes in the O'Reilly Auto Parts race and the Truck Series also takes to the track.

Pit stall assignments have been released for teams competing in the weekend events. The races feature both veteran drivers and rising stars in NASCAR competition. All three series races will be broadcast on television throughout the weekend.

cards.headline: Sacramento launches bid for Major League Baseball expansion team
cards.teaser: A Sacramento investment group has begun pursuing a Major League Baseball expansion franchise, joining other cities seeking new teams.
cards.body:
Sacramento has formally entered the competition for MLB expansion, with local investors assembling a bid package. The effort includes notable financial backers, though some potential investors have already withdrawn from the group.

The Sacramento bid joins expansion efforts from Vancouver, Tampa, and other cities seeking Major League Baseball franchises. Local fans have expressed enthusiasm for bringing professional baseball to California's capital city. MLB has not announced a timeline for expansion decisions or how many new franchises the league might add.

cards.headline: Glasgow Warriors advance to URC semifinals with win over Connacht
cards.teaser: Glasgow Warriors defeated Connacht to reach the United Rugby Championship semifinals, where they will face either Bulls or Munster.
cards.body:
Glasgow Warriors advanced to the United Rugby Championship semi-finals with a hard-fought victory over Connacht. The win secures their place in the final four of the competition and keeps their championship ambitions on track.

The Warriors will face either Bulls or Munster in the semi-finals, depending on the outcome of that quarterfinal matchup. Glasgow's battling performance against Connacht proved decisive in their path through the playoffs.

hero.headline: Marcia Lucas, Oscar-Winning Star Wars Editor, Dies at 80
hero.body:
Marcia Lucas, the film editor who won an Academy Award for editing Star Wars, died Wednesday in Rancho Mirage, California. She was 80.

The family's attorney confirmed she died of cancer. Lucas edited the original 1977 Star Wars film directed by her former husband George Lucas.

Lucas shaped several influential films of the 1970s beyond Star Wars. Her editing work also included American Graffiti, contributing to the success of multiple landmark films from that era.

She won the Oscar for her editing work on Star Wars, which became one of the most successful and culturally significant films in cinema history. Her contributions to the film helped establish its pacing and narrative structure.

The family's attorney described her as a brilliant storyteller and a trailblazer in the film industry. Lucas worked during a time when few women held prominent editing positions in major Hollywood productions.

Lucas was married to George Lucas during the production of his early films. The couple later divorced, but her professional legacy remained tied to the films that defined a generation of moviegoers.

Her editing career demonstrated technical skill and narrative instinct that influenced how science fiction and adventure films were constructed. The success of Star Wars helped establish new standards for pacing and visual storytelling in Hollywood.

Lucas lived in Rancho Mirage in her later years. She had been battling cancer before her death on Wednesday.

Beyond her Oscar win, Lucas's work on American Graffiti also earned recognition. That film, released in 1973, became a critical and commercial success that helped launch George Lucas's directing career before Star Wars.

Her death marks the loss of a key figure from the creative team behind some of the most memorable films of the 1970s. The editing techniques she employed on Star Wars influenced generations of editors who followed.

cards.headline: Over Half of Great American State Fair Performers Drop Out
cards.teaser: Multiple artists have withdrawn from a Trump-backed concert celebrating America's 250th anniversary.
cards.body:
More than half of the scheduled performers for the Great American State Fair have withdrawn from the event. The concert is part of the Freedom 250 series, positioned as an alternative to the official America250 celebration of the nation's 250th birthday.

Artists cited political concerns and threats as reasons for their departures from the summer event.

cards.headline: Frankie Valli Cancels Remaining 2026 Concerts
cards.teaser: The 92-year-old singer announced he is canceling all tour dates for the rest of the year due to health issues.
cards.body:
Frankie Valli announced Friday that he is canceling all remaining concert dates for 2026 due to health issues. The 92-year-old singer said he needs to focus on his health at this time.

Valli expressed his apologies to fans who purchased tickets to his shows. Despite the cancellation, he reaffirmed his enduring passion for performing and touring.

cards.headline: Olivia Rodrigo Announces New Album Release Date and Tracklist
cards.teaser: The singer's new album, titled You Seem Pretty Sad For a Girl So in Love, will be released on June 12.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo revealed the tracklist for her upcoming album You Seem Pretty Sad For a Girl So in Love. The album will be released on June 12.

Rodrigo said the album assesses a relationship from beginning to breakup. She described one song as the thesis statement for the album's themes. The new release represents a milestone in her recording career.

cards.headline: A24's Backrooms Earns Over $10 Million in Previews
cards.teaser: The horror film directed by 20-year-old Kane Parsons is now in theaters nationwide.
cards.body:
Backrooms, the debut feature from 20-year-old director Kane Parsons, has grossed more than $10 million during preview screenings. The A24 horror film is now playing in theaters nationwide and is positioned to be a major box office success.

The film features an ensemble cast including Chiwetel Ejiofor, Renate Reinsve, Mark Duplass, Avan Jogia, Finn Bennett, and Lukita Maxwell. The movie draws inspiration from an original YouTube series of the same name.

cards.headline: Kanye West Approved to Perform in Netherlands
cards.teaser: Officials cleared the rapper to enter the country for a birthday performance after finding insufficient evidence to ban him.
cards.body:
Kanye West has been cleared to perform in the Netherlands on his birthday. Dutch officials ruled that insufficient evidence existed to ban the rapper from entering the country.

The decision allows West to proceed with his planned performance. Officials had previously considered whether to block his entry but determined they could not support such a ban.

cards.headline: Los Angeles Councilwoman Urges Governor Candidates to Support Film Tax Credits
cards.teaser: Nithya Raman called for uncapped tax incentives for film and TV production in California.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Councilwoman Nithya Raman urged candidates for governor to support uncapped tax incentives for film and TV production. She made the call Friday outside Radford Studios with entertainment industry figures.

Raman appeared with Mike Schur, Cord Jefferson, and Kay Cannon, who support her mayoral campaign. She said California must ensure Hollywood remains competitive. The primary election is scheduled for Tuesday.

hero.headline: Judge orders Trump's name removed from Kennedy Center
hero.body:
A federal judge in Washington, D.C. ruled that President Trump's name must be removed from the Kennedy Center, blocking the administration's planned renovation of the performing arts venue.

U.S. District Judge signed the order requiring Trump's name to be stripped from the building and surrounding signage within two weeks. The ruling also halted the scheduled closure of the facility, which had been set to shut down later this year to begin work.

The judge wrote in a 94-page decision that it was crystal clear the arts complex was named for President John F. Kennedy. The court found that the Kennedy Center's board exceeded its legal authority by acting on its own to rename the facility.

The ruling prevents the center from winding down its programming and closing for what had been planned as a two-year renovation period. The decision represents a setback for the Trump administration's plans to overhaul the venue.

The Kennedy Center serves as the nation's cultural center and memorial to President Kennedy, who was assassinated in 1963. Congress established the center through legislation that designated it as a living memorial to the 35th president.

The court determined that the board lacked statutory power to unilaterally change the name of the federally chartered institution. The judge's order applies to all Trump branding that had been added to the building and its grounds.

The administration now faces a deadline to comply with the removal order while its renovation plans remain on hold. The ruling leaves open questions about whether and how the planned improvements to the facility might proceed under its original name.

cards.headline: Pentagon awards Dell $9.7 billion contract amid Trump stock holdings
cards.teaser: The Defense Department signed a five-year agreement with Dell for Microsoft software and cloud services after President Trump promoted the company and purchased its stock.
cards.body:
The Pentagon announced a $9.7 billion contract with Dell for Microsoft software and cloud services as part of an effort to consolidate its technology infrastructure. The five-year agreement was announced on a recent weekday.

The deal has prompted questions about potential conflicts of interest. President Trump had previously promoted Dell products and purchased significant amounts of the company's stock before the Defense Department awarded the contract.

cards.headline: Judge reopens Trump's $10 billion IRS lawsuit
cards.teaser: A federal judge in Florida sided with outside parties who challenged a settlement between the Trump administration and the Justice Department.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Florida agreed to reopen President Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against the IRS. Intervenors in the case argued that a settlement agreement to establish an "anti-weaponization" fund had compromised the proceedings. The judge's decision allows the case to proceed despite the prior agreement between the Justice Department and Trump to voluntarily dismiss the suit.

The ruling enables further examination of Trump's claims against the tax agency.

cards.headline: New Jersey detention center becomes test for DHS Secretary Mullin
cards.teaser: Protests and a reported hunger strike at Delaney Hall mark the first major immigration clash under the new Homeland Security chief.
cards.body:
A private detention center in Newark, New Jersey has become a flashpoint in disputes over Trump administration immigration policies. The situation represents the first major test for Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin.

Protesters have been arrested outside the facility while detainees reportedly participate in a hunger strike. The detainees cite claims of inhumane living conditions and inadequate medical care. The 1,000-bed Delaney Hall Facility reopened last year and has since been the site of ongoing tension.

cards.headline: Trump endorses Evette over Rep. Mace in South Carolina governor race
cards.teaser: The president backed Lt. Gov. Pam Evette instead of Rep. Nancy Mace in the Republican primary contest.
cards.body:
President Trump endorsed Lt. Gov. Pam Evette in the South Carolina governor race on Friday, backing her over Rep. Nancy Mace's campaign for the position. Trump announced his support on Truth Social, describing Evette as an "America First Patriot" who has remained steadfast in her commitment.

In his endorsement statement, Trump praised Evette as a good friend, fighter, and winner. The endorsement represents a notable snub to Mace, the sitting congressman who is seeking to move to the governor's office.

cards.headline: Treasury Secretary supports putting Trump on proposed $250 bill
cards.teaser: Scott Bessent endorsed featuring the president on a commemorative bill for the nation's 250th anniversary.
cards.body:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that the White House is pushing Congress to approve a $250 bill featuring President Trump's portrait to commemorate the country's 250th anniversary of independence. The treasury department has already begun preparing for the possibility of issuing the new currency.

The proposal would require changing federal law that currently prohibits any living person from appearing on U.S. currency. Democrats have vowed to block the move, while the treasury secretary defended the initiative as a way to celebrate the nation's semiquincentennial.

cards.headline: Talarico leads Paxton by 3 points in Texas governor poll
cards.teaser: A survey of likely voters shows the Democratic state representative ahead of the Republican attorney general.
cards.body:
State Rep. James Talarico holds a narrow lead over Attorney General Ken Paxton in the Texas governor race, according to a poll released by Texas Public Opinion Research. Talarico drew support from 47 percent of likely general election voters compared to 44 percent for Paxton.

The survey measured voter preferences following the runoff election. The three-point margin represents a slight edge for the Democratic candidate over his Republican opponent in the contest.
